title.value: Guided Interpretable Facial Expression Recognition via Spatial Action Unit Cues
title.justification: The title clearly suggests that the paper deals with facial expression recognition using spatial action unit cues for interpretability.
title.quote: Guided Interpretable Facial Expression Recognition via Spatial Action Unit Cues

analysis.description: This paper proposes a new learning strategy for facial expression recognition that incorporates spatial action unit (AU) cues into classifier training, improving interpretability without degrading classification performance. The strategy is applied to deep CNN- or transformer-based classifiers on public benchmarks like RAF-DB and AffectNet.

type.justification: The paper involves extensive evaluation and experimentation on two public benchmarks, RAF-DB and AffectNet, to demonstrate the improvement in classification and interpretability.
type.quote: Our extensive evaluation 1 on two public benchmarks RAF-DB, and AffectNet datasets shows that our proposed strategy can improve layer-wise interpretability without degrading classification performance.

name.justification: The primary focus of the paper is on facial expression recognition, with an emphasis on interpretability using spatial action unit cues.
name.quote: Although state-of-the-art classifiers for facial expression recognition (FER) can achieve a high level of accuracy, they lack interpretability, an important feature for end-users.

name.justification: The paper introduces a method to enhance the interpretability of classifiers used in facial expression recognition by incorporating spatial AU cues.
name.quote: This paper introduces a generic learning strategy to build an interpretable deep classifier for the FER task.

name.justification: APVIT is mentioned as a recent state-of-the-art method building spatial attention for facial expression recognition but does not directly contribute to this paper.
name.quote: Recent progress with attention-based methods like APVIT [82] allows extracting internal attention explicitly to select only discriminative regions of interest (ROIs).

is_contributed.justification: APVIT is referenced as part of the related works but not introduced as a part of this research.
is_contributed.quote: In the FER task, we selected a recent state-of-the-art method, APVIT [82], which builds spatial attention in its architecture to yield interpretable maps.

is_executed.justification: The execution or implementation details of APVIT are not provided in the paper. It is merely mentioned among state-of-the-art methods.
is_executed.quote: ...APVIT [82]...it does not have a CAM module.

is_compared.justification: APVIT is only mentioned in passing and not directly compared numerically in the results section.
is_compared.quote: Note that achieving better classification accuracy does not necessarily translate to better interpretability. For instance, the vanilla APVIT method [82] has the highest classification accuracy CL of 91% over RAF-DB.
